belongs_to: Section 9.1, page no. 219, Figure it Out Q2: 'For each of the following figures, identify the line(s) of symmetry if it exists.' (printed answer, figure 1 of 3, the bent/folded-paper shape on the left)
description: Outline polygon with 6 vertices, concave, like a sheet of paper folded along a crease and seen at an angle: it is two congruent four-sided halves joined along a crease. Vertices in drawing order: lower-left vertex A, then up to B (upper-left), then along the top edge to C (upper-right, the highest point), then down-left to a notch vertex D (concave vertex in the middle of the right side), then out to E (right-most vertex, lower than C), then down-left to F (bottom vertex), then back to A. One dashed line is drawn through vertex A and the notch vertex D (it rises to the right at roughly 25 degrees) and it extends beyond the shape at both ends (a little below-left of A and a little above-right of D). That dashed line is the line of symmetry: B and F, and C and E, are mirror images across it. Black outline, no fill, no labels.
